title: Product vocabulary and user-facing language
affectedPackages: Identity Directory for Organization and Person
versioning: contracts/vocabulary/terms.json and this record share one revision counter, so vocabulary@<n> is DR-0001@<n>. Any change to terms.json takes a new revision marked additive (new terms, aliases, or label options) or breaking (a removed or renamed term, alias, or label option, or a changed visibility). The check compares terms.json with main: a change that keeps main's revision fails VOCAB_REVISION_NOT_BUMPED, a removal not marked breaking fails VOCAB_COMPATIBILITY_UNDECLARED, and a breaking revision keeps a term adapter entry for each removed name. A ratified revision pins the SHA-256 of terms.json in approvalRef, so an unapproved edit fails DR_APPROVAL_STALE.
supersession: A ratified revision is never edited. A wrong decision gets a new revision that names the prior one in supersedes (DR-0001@<n>) and gives supersessionReason; consumers re-cite, and #17's LEAF_GATE_SUPERSEDED flags citations of a superseded breaking revision. An unratified revision can be reverted.
context: The vocabulary lived only in the rounds-review spec. This record makes the registry the one source for product and domain names: terms.json (governed here), adapters.json (baseline names and the leaves that retire them), leaf-ids.json (every citable leaf ID), and the generated docs/vocabulary.md and frontend/src/vocabulary/labels.ts.

securityConsequences.account: No runtime or account-scope change. Definitions restate spec 384-391: every canonical record belongs to a server-derived account.
securityConsequences.privacy: The five privacy classes are named here and defined by #72 (ROUNDS-14-L01); nothing here relaxes a class. Term examples must be synthetic.
securityConsequences.secret: Secret appears only as a privacy class (spec 2147). The check rejects bearer-shaped tokens, /r/ share URLs, and email addresses outside example.com in term examples, and no secret value is recorded.
securityConsequences.publicBoundary: Share Capability is labeled "Share link"; nothing here changes what a public share resolves (spec 2584-2636). The repository is public, and the registry holds only names, definitions, and paths.

decisions.title: Transcribe the approved spec; spec text wins
decisions.decision: Terms, definitions, and labels are transcribed from spec 221-228, 415-425, 623-645, 752-811, 815-840, 966-1017, and 2491-2636, and only the gaps below are decided here. Where rounds-review src/data/glossary.ts differs, spec text wins: glossary.ts drops "according to stage" from the Pursuit label (spec 1004), and the registry keeps it.

alternatives.option: Use glossary.ts as the label source
alternatives.reason: It drops "according to stage" (spec 1004) and returns the internal term for an unknown name, which the label contract forbids.
No approval basis; the spec is the approved artifact.

decisions.consequences: Every term cites the spec lines it comes from. A later spec change reaches the registry only through a new revision.
decisions.rollbackImpact: Revert an unratified revision; supersede a ratified one.

decisions.title: Name every version in the authority matrix
decisions.decision: The revision vocabulary (spec 754-764) adds the matrix versions: Opportunity Revision (786), Relation Version (793), Edition Version (794), Preference Version (802), Key Version (808), Activation Version (809), Capability Version (810), Projection Watermark (800, 811), and Algorithm Version (800, 801; also 811's "Projector version"). Entity Version aliases 781's "Provider/session version" and 782's "Profile/Entity Version"; Aggregate Revision aliases 789's "Expected-version command history" and 790's "Append-only accepted revision".

alternatives.option: Keep only the nine terms in spec 754-764
alternatives.reason: Matrix cells (781-811) would name versions no term defines, and #16's rows cite terms.

alternatives.option: Fold every version into Entity Version
alternatives.reason: Watermarks and algorithm versions are not concurrency tokens; one name would hide different rules.

decisions.consequences: Each version cell in #16's matrix resolves to a term. The added versions are internal or inspection-only and carry no label.
decisions.migrationImpact: None. Leaves that implement a version use these names.
decisions.rollbackImpact: Superseding revision; removed names keep adapter entries.

decisions.title: Interview Round and Practice Item
decisions.decision: Interview Round is a Career Activity kind (spec 1497): "Interview Round" resolves to Career Activity, labeled with the kind option "Interview". Practice Item is pack-owned practice content keyed (pack, track, slug) per #39 (ROUNDS-07-L01), and #130 (ROUNDS-28-L01) owns the term. ai_coding_rounds rows are Practice Items.

alternatives.option: Make Interview Round its own aggregate
alternatives.reason: Career Activity is the sole mutable authority for schedules (spec 488-503); a second aggregate recreates the split.

alternatives.option: Treat AI-coding rounds as interview rounds
alternatives.reason: They are practice content, not dated occurrences.

decisions.consequences: "Round" alone is never a label. interview_rounds maps to Career Activity and ai_coding_rounds to Practice Item.
decisions.migrationImpact: #110 (ROUNDS-22-L05) migrates interview rounds; #43 (ROUNDS-07-L05) adopts the content collections.

decisions.title: Claim and Attempt
decisions.decision: "Claim" aliases Extracted Claim (spec 834). "Attempt" labels only Practice Attempt (spec 1013). Execution Attempt (#3, ROUNDS-00A-L03) and Processing Attempt (spec 706, 803, 1168) are inspection-only.

alternatives.reason: Three different records would share one user-facing word.

alternatives.option: Register Claim as its own term
alternatives.reason: Spec 834's Claim is the platform name of the same record.

decisions.consequences: A usage rule rejects "Attempt" as a label on any other term.

decisions.title: The Profile page is Account
decisions.decision: The current Profile page is Account (spec 405, 987). "Profile" alone is never a label; Career Profile is the only profile.

alternatives.reason: Spec 405-406 and 987 move it to Account and keep professional facts in Career Profile.
Same collision with Career Profile.

decisions.consequences: The Profile page header, its menu item, and the /profile and /settings segments get adapters that #178 retires.
decisions.migrationImpact: #178 replaces the copy; #25 (ROUNDS-03-L02) decides users.name, users.bio, and users.target.

decisions.title: Labels the spec gives two terms
decisions.decision: sharedLabels holds every option the spec gives two terms: "Role" (Opportunity 1003, Engagement 418) and "Opportunity" (Opportunity 1003, Pursuit 1004). "Role" stays as written, and SCR-ROLE asks the owner for distinct labels.

alternatives.reason: That departs from spec text, so it goes to the owner as a spec-change request.
The spec itself shares these two.

decisions.consequences: The duplicate-label check exempts exactly these pairs.
decisions.rollbackImpact: Superseding revision once the owner rules on SCR-ROLE.

decisions.title: Workspace means the Opportunity Workspace
decisions.decision: In UI copy, "workspace" means only the Opportunity Workspace (spec 989, 1433).

alternatives.reason: Spec 978 and 295-296 make a campaign a lens, not a workspace boundary.
The spec names the Opportunity Workspace.

decisions.consequences: Baseline campaign copy that says workspace (the Command Center entry, docs/architecture.md) gets adapters, and a usage rule rejects "workspace" in any other label.
decisions.migrationImpact: None; retiring leaves rewrite the copy.
decisions.rollbackImpact: The owner can change it; a superseding revision updates the rule and its adapters.

decisions.title: Setting, Provider, Capability, and X or Y
decisions.decision: Account preferences are labeled "Setting"; "Preference" stays with the profile construct (Preference or Constraint). "Provider" is always qualified: Sign-in provider, AI provider, Calendar provider. In UI copy, "Capability" means only Share Capability. In "X or Y", the first name is canonical and the second is a label option.

alternatives.reason: The profile construct (spec 425) and Account preference (spec 802) would collide.
Sign-in, AI, and calendar providers are different things with different privacy rules.

alternatives.option: Use "Capability" for pack required capabilities in UI copy
alternatives.reason: That is an internal manifest field (spec 862).

decisions.consequences: Labels Setting, Sign-in provider, AI provider, and Calendar provider; usage rules reject bare Preference, Provider, and Capability labels.
decisions.rollbackImpact: The owner can change it; superseding revision.

decisions.title: Labels for terms the spec leaves unlabeled
decisions.decision: A user-facing term the spec does not label takes its canonical term, a spec 966-974 destination, or its baseline label. Share Capability keeps the baseline "Share link".

alternatives.reason: No approval basis.

alternatives.option: Leave them unlabeled and fall back to the internal term
alternatives.reason: The label contract has no internal-term fallback.

decisions.consequences: Every user-facing term has a label, and label() never returns an internal name.
decisions.rollbackImpact: The owner can change any label; a superseding revision keeps adapters for the old ones.

decisions.title: Software Engineering track names
decisions.decision: System Design, Coding, AI-Assisted Coding, Take-Home, and Behavioral live in a provisional pack.software-engineering namespace, with baseline spellings ("AI Assisted Coding", "Real World Problems", "Real-World Problem", real-world, builder, system) as aliases, until #39 takes the namespace over under pack ID software-engineering.

alternatives.reason: Practice tracks belong to a pack (spec 855, 937-943), and a non-engineering pack must not inherit them.
Surfaces and adapters need the names now.

decisions.consequences: Track labels are namespaced, and the pack-collision check applies to them.
decisions.migrationImpact: #39 adopts the namespace; #43 maps track and round-type keys.
decisions.rollbackImpact: Superseding revision; #39 can rename with adapters.

decisions.title: Disposition vocabulary
decisions.decision: Features take Preserve, Transform, or owner-approved Retire (spec 335-337) plus an optional qualifier (spec 341-374). Data items take migrate, archive, rebuild, reconcile, or drop (spec 2666-2670). For #155 (ROUNDS-32-L01): bridge is migrate with a time-bounded adapter the transferring leaf owns, quarantine is archive, and retire is an owner-approved drop.

alternatives.option: One flat list for features and items
alternatives.reason: The two levels answer different questions: a feature can Transform while its items migrate, rebuild, or archive.
bridge, quarantine, and retire are not spec dispositions.

decisions.consequences: The disposition parser reads all 34 ledger rows as Preserve or Transform plus a qualifier.
decisions.migrationImpact: #155's inventory rows use the item values.

decisions.title: Data-preserving clean cutover
decisions.decision: "Data-preserving clean cutover" follows spec 2637-2647: one bounded context at a time, one writable authority per converted concept, an explicit retirement criterion, and a time-bounded compatibility window. The two shipped migration comments that use the unqualified phrase for a drop with no data migration are allowlisted, not edited, because #1's lint (ROUNDS-00A-L01) bars editing shipped migrations. A new unqualified use fails.

alternatives.reason: Shipped migrations are immutable.
It names data loss after the approved strategy, which means the opposite.

decisions.consequences: VOCAB_CUTOVER_UNQUALIFIED fails a new unqualified use outside the allowlist.

decisions.title: Containment terms
decisions.decision: The five containment terms (Legacy Artifact Snapshot, Test Definition, Harness Revision, Artifact Renderer Contract, Share Capability) come from spec 623-645, 2491-2636, and 3212. If #2, #3, #4, or #11 merges first with a different shipped name, the registry adopts it and lists each difference as a spec-change item. At revision 1 none of them has merged and no containment collection exists (the only ROUNDS-00 work on next comes from #1 and #9), so the spec names stand and there is no spec-change item.

alternatives.reason: They need names to cite now.
The spec names are approved.

decisions.consequences: Containment leaves cite these term IDs. Execution Attempt (#3) is inspection-only under G3.
decisions.rollbackImpact: A containment leaf that ships another name supersedes this revision with a spec-change item.

decisions.title: Positioning
decisions.decision: The positioning statement is PRODUCT.md line 45, and its title form is "Career Command Center". This leaf rewrites README.md lines 1 and 3 and docs/architecture.md line 3 to it. frontend/index.html:17, Login.tsx:239, and SHOWCASE.md:3 keep adapter entries until #164 (ROUNDS-32-L10).

alternatives.reason: PRODUCT.md positions Rounds as a career command center.
Two are UI strings that retiring leaves own, and this leaf changes no UI string.

decisions.consequences: VOCAB_POSITIONING_STALE fails a positioning line that matches neither the statement nor its adapter entry.
decisions.rollbackImpact: Revert the two doc lines; the adapters stay.

decisions.title: Coverage set and adapter entries
decisions.decision: Every coverage-set name maps to a term label or an adapter entry: the 40 live and 3 historical collections, the user_progress.question_type and status values, the INTERVIEW_TYPES keys of interview_rounds.round_type, runner router prefixes and /health, literal App.tsx segments, Layout navigation labels and Command Center entries, literal eyebrow and title props at the 24 AppHeader call sites, and the six positioning lines. Retiring leaves: #110 for interview_rounds and its round types, #178 for the Profile and Settings pages, #43 for the nine content collections it adopts, the owning surface leaf for page, shell, and Command Center copy, and #164 by default. #25 decides users.target.

alternatives.reason: Retiring leaves do that; renaming here would break stored data and links.
Baseline collisions would stay invisible.

decisions.consequences: VOCAB_UNCOVERED_NAME fails a new uncovered name; add the adapter entry, never loosen the rule. VOCAB_ADAPTER_STALE fails an entry whose name is gone, so the retiring leaf removes it.
decisions.migrationImpact: None. Adapter entries change no stored data.
decisions.rollbackImpact: Adapter entries are data outside the governed file; edit or revert them without a new vocabulary revision.

decisions.title: Label module
decisions.decision: frontend/src/vocabulary/labels.ts exports a TermId union of user-facing terms, label(termId, { option, count }), inspectionTerms for inspection surfaces (spec 1016-1017), and specLabels with the spec 1000-1014 labels as written. There is no internal-term fallback: an unknown or internal term throws. New UI code imports it; existing copy keeps its adapter until its retiring leaf replaces it.

alternatives.reason: It returns the internal term for an unknown name.
Out of scope; retiring leaves own each surface.

decisions.consequences: labels.ts changes no rendered string until a surface imports it. #173 checks rendered strings and #170 checks UI literals for internal terms.

corrections.title: Move the export gate to ROUNDS-01 closure
corrections.detail: The filed export gate (database ADR and ERD; command contracts; authorization matrix, Audit Entry, and event catalogue; product and leaf non-goals plus a reference issue) comes from #18 to #22 (ROUNDS-02-L01 to L05) and the rest of #17's gate table. #18's filed edge on #17 closes a cycle through this leaf, so per spec 3195-3197 ("before completing ROUNDS-01") the gate moves to ROUNDS-01 closure for #15 to #17.

corrections.title: Make this leaf a prerequisite wherever a body lists it
corrections.detail: Every revised body that lists ROUNDS-01-L01 gets it as a prerequisite, not only #16 and #17. #17's docs/program/leaf-dag.json carries the full edge list.

corrections.title: #170 adopts the conformance job
corrections.detail: #170 (ROUNDS-34-L01) adopts this job and rule interface, adds the internal-term rule, and takes #8's (ROUNDS-00A-L08) job, alert, and ruleset entry as containment-corpus.

corrections.title: Stage labels and routes have their own owners
corrections.detail: #99 (ROUNDS-20-L01) owns the stage-to-label mapping. #165 (ROUNDS-33-L01) owns routes and takes labels from here.

corrections.title: The collection rule moves to #155
corrections.detail: The collection extraction in rules/vocabulary.mjs moves to #155 (ROUNDS-32-L01) once its store registry lands.

corrections.title: Spec-change requests and ratified-here decisions
corrections.detail: The Role and Submission spec-change requests (SCR-ROLE, SCR-SUBMISSION) and every ratified-here decision (G6 to G9) need the owner to approve or change them.

specChangeRequests.title: Distinct labels for Opportunity and Engagement
specChangeRequests.detail: Spec 1003 labels Opportunity "Opportunity or Role" and spec 418 names the profile construct "Engagement or Role", so "Role" names two things. The owner picks distinct labels; until then both keep "Role" (G5).

specChangeRequests.title: Add "Submission" to the Career Activity labels
specChangeRequests.detail: #88 (ROUNDS-17-L04) and #107 (ROUNDS-22-L02) label material-submission activities "Submission", which spec 1011 ("Interview, Conversation, Follow-up, or Activity") lacks; #107 also has no follow-up kind because #113 uses Actions. labels.ts carries spec 1011 as written until the owner amends it.

departures.title: Issue drafts (original AC 2)
departures.detail: Original AC 2 asks issue drafts to use the same definitions. This leaf edits no issue body; filed bodies that use other names reach the owner through #17's re-authorization, which imports this file (re-authorization item 7).

departures.title: Positioning title form
departures.detail: PRODUCT.md line 45 gives the statement. Titles use its noun phrase, "Career Command Center": README.md line 1 now, and the index.html and Login.tsx targets later.

departures.title: Spec over glossary.ts
departures.detail: rounds-review src/data/glossary.ts drops "according to stage" from the Pursuit label and falls back to the internal term. The registry keeps spec 1004's text, and label() has no fallback.

departures.title: Layout and Command Center coverage
departures.detail: The check reads Layout's navigation labels, user-menu destinations, and sidebar headings, and each Command Center entry's label and description. Accessible names and the forms inside Command Center views are outside it; #173 checks rendered strings.

departures.title: Retiring leaves beyond the three the body names
departures.detail: Besides #110, #178, and the #164 default, adapters name #43 for the nine content collections it adopts and the owning surface leaf for page, shell, and Command Center copy (#26, #81, #101, #105, #128, #132 to #136, #166, #168), per #165's and #168's ownership lists.
